newsitem.title: UK: Oil price in neutral assessing U.S. gasoline demand.
newsitem.headline: Oil price in neutral assessing U.S. gasoline demand.

text.p: Oil markets stayed in neutral gear again on Thursday, engine idling while traders assessed seasonal spring demand growth for U.S. gasoline.
Bellwether North Sea Brent blend at 1600 GMT had gained just two cents to $18.54 a barrel.
Demand from U.S. motorists remains key to the short-term future of the oil markets, but traders are having difficulty deciding whether the outlook is bullish, bearish or plain neutral.
Gasoline prices got a little help this week from weekly U.S. statistics showing a small fall in stocks last week.
"Inventories slipped a little and even though they're lower than this time last year there seems to be no fear of a shortage of supply in the market," said a trader.
Higher refinery run rates ahead of the peak gasoline season are helping to support crude prices, with cargoes of West African and North Sea oil flooding into the U.S. Gulf refining centre.
But strong supply growth threatens to push prices lower again in the medium term unless gasoline demand accelerates, dealers said.
Concern over Iran's diplomatic standoff with the European Union also has helped staunch the 30 percent slide in crude values which took Brent to a nine-month low at $17.54 at the beginning of April.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Thursday denounced Iran's refusal to accept the return of its ambassador and said his country would not submit to "blackmail"

He suggested EU countries would not now send their ambassadors back after their withdrawal earlier this month when a German court implicated senior Iranian officials in the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
A meeting of EU foreign ministers this week agreed to send the ambassadors back but suspended ministerial contacts.
